title: Personal Website

bodiesOfWork.title: Spatial Webflow predecessor
bodiesOfWork.summary: A spatial portfolio built with Webflow, CSS, JavaScript, sound, motion, and CSS-based 3D.

bodiesOfWork.title: Current React studio website
bodiesOfWork.summary: The current framed, route-based studio site and simulation system that evolved from the predecessor's performance and structure lessons.
bodiesOfWork.notes: Register the current repository and implementation history as direct evidence before confirming facts.

workingHypotheses: Portfolio v1 documents a predecessor built with Webflow, CSS, and JavaScript; the final case study should tell the evolution into the current React and simulation system rather than polishing the obsolete version.

organisingIdea.statement: Treat the browser's limitations as a creative collaborator that determines which expressive ideas deserve to survive.

claims.statement: The predecessor site explored whether a personal website could feel like a spatial environment rather than a sequence of pages.
claims.notes: Confirm whether this remains the core question of the current site.

claims.statement: The site functioned as a portfolio and professional introduction for prospective collaborators, clients, and employers.
claims.notes: Ask which audience actually mattered most.

claims.statement: Portfolio v1 labels the predecessor as a 2024–ongoing project in May 2025.
claims.notes: Current project history and major rebuild dates still need to be established.

claims.statement: Alexander was the designer and developer of the predecessor site.
claims.notes: The current site's AI-assisted development and any collaborators should be credited separately.

claims.statement: The predecessor was built with Webflow, native CSS, and JavaScript and used custom motion, layout, sound, and CSS-based 3D.
claims.notes: Historical implementation only; do not describe the current repo this way.

claims.statement: Canvas animation, ambient layers, concurrent scripts, mobile memory, and rendering bottlenecks forced performance to become a design constraint.
claims.notes: Likely still relevant, but current examples should come from the live implementation history.

claims.statement: Early experiments were removed when they felt too heavy, ornamental, or disconnected from the intended spatial rhythm.
claims.notes: Ask for two rejected examples and the rule learned from each.

claims.statement: Generative tools were used to imagine textures, lighting, and environments, with outputs interpreted and manually refined rather than treated as final design.
claims.notes: Identify which tools and outputs materially influenced the current site.

claims.statement: The predecessor used horizontal movement, parallax depth, and arrival-like transitions to make the interface feel spatial.
claims.notes: Compare this explicitly with the current framed-window and simulation language.

claims.statement: The old portfolio says refactoring made the predecessor leaner, more modular, documented, and able to grow, while work remained ongoing.
claims.notes: Treat as a reflection, not a measured outcome.

conflicts.question: Which predecessor concepts survive in the current site, and which should be documented only as discarded history?
The factsheet carries S&P collaborator credits that appear copied; confirm that these are not personal-site credits.
